source_block.parva: Shanti Parva, Rajadharmanushasana sub-parva (vulgate §1–§53; BORI CE ch. 1–~51): the month of mourning by the Ganga; Yudhishthira's grief and wish to renounce; the counsel of Arjuna, Bhima, Draupadi, Vyasa and Krishna (the Shodasharajika); the entry into Hastinapura and the coronation; Krishna's meditation on Bhishma; the visit to Bhishma on his bed of arrows
source_block.bori: BORI CE Shanti Parva, Rajadharmanushasana sub-parva, Debroy translation vol. 8 (chapter-group citations): month of mourning by the Ganga and Kunti's consolation; Yudhishthira resolves to go to the forest and tells Arjuna to rule; Arjuna and Bhima on a king's duty to act; Draupadi's plea; Vyasa on the householder's and king's dharma; Krishna takes his hand and tells of the sixteen kings; the coronation, Krishna pouring the conch water; Krishna's meditation on Bhishma; the visit to Bhishma and Krishna's boon freeing him from pain.
source_block.gita_press: Gita Press Gorakhpur Mahabharata (Hindi, vulgate numbering = Ganguli): Shanti Parva, Rajadharmanushasana Parva adhyayas 1, 6 (Ganga-tat, Kunti ki saantvana), 7 (van jaane ka nishchay), 8, 10 (Arjuna, Bhimsen), 14 (Draupadi), 23, 32 (Vyasa), 29 (Shri Krishna, solah raja), 37–41 (Hastinapur pravesh, rajyabhishek), 46–47 (Shri Krishna ka dhyan), 51–52 (Bhishma ke paas; vardaan).
source_block.divergence: Section/adhyaya numbers follow the vulgate (Ganguli = Gita Press); BORI CE chapters are cited at chapter-group level only (the CE drops and merges some vulgate chapters). Omitted for length: Narada's account of Karna's curses (§1–§5), the speeches of Nakula, Sahadeva, Devasthana and others, the tale of the rakshasa Charvaka slain by the Brahmanas' curse (§38–§39), Bhima made yuvaraja and the other appointments (§41), the palaces given to the brothers, the Bhishmastavaraja hymn (§47), Rama Jamadagnya's story told on the way (§48–§49), and Krishna's long praise of Bhishma. In the texts Arjuna, Bhima, the twins, Satyaki and others go with Krishna and Yudhishthira to Bhishma; the bedside plate shows only Krishna, Yudhishthira and Bhishma. Dhaumya prepares the altar and Dhritarashtra and the people also anoint the king; the crown plate shows only Krishna's conch-pouring with Draupadi beside the king. The 'meditate' line condenses Krishna's words in §46.
source_block.chosen: Gita Press + BORI/Debroy overlap: the month by the Ganga; Yudhishthira's grief for Karna and Kunti's consolation; his wish to give up the kingdom and tell Arjuna to rule; Arjuna and Bhima on a king's duty to act; Draupadi's plea; Vyasa's counsel that the forest is not his path and a king must protect his people; Krishna takes his hand and tells of the kings of old; the coronation with Draupadi beside him and Krishna pouring the conch water; Krishna's meditation on Bhishma; Krishna leads Yudhishthira to Bhishma and asks him to teach and dispel the king's grief; Krishna's boon freeing Bhishma from pain.
